hints.title: Base Representation Analysis
hints.text: Consider the representation of number n in base b = n - 2.

hints.title: Leading and Trailing Digits
hints.text: For any n >= 4, expressing n in base n - 2 always gives quotient 1 with remainder 2, which produces the two-digit string '12'.

hints.title: Impossibility Invariant
hints.text: Since '12' is never palindromic, no integer n >= 4 can ever be strictly palindromic across all bases from 2 up to n - 2.

hints.title: Constant Time Invariant Implementation

complexity.notes: Mathematical proof guarantees false for all n >= 4.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Base conversion for all b in range [2, n-2] incurs unnecessary O(n log n) overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) logic with zero state allocation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Analyzes the base n - 2 representation to deduce that returning false is universally optimal.
